Operations / Reliability and oversight

Automation outcome success rate

A configured business-outcome measure: the percentage of eligible automated job attempts that finish with a validated expected outcome. A workflow status of successful is checked against the intended result, such as a correctly created CRM record.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

A configured business-outcome measure: the percentage of eligible automated job attempts that finish with a validated expected outcome. A workflow status of successful is checked against the intended result, such as a correctly created CRM record.

%

How we use it

We attach outcome checks and alerts to workflows so the team can inspect failed actions and recover affected records rather than relying only on technical execution status.

Transparent calculationEligible job attempts with validated successful outcomes ÷ all eligible terminal job attempts × 100
validated successful attempts970
all terminal attempts1,000

970 ÷ 1,000 × 100 = 97% successful outcomes across completed attempts.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Job type and workflow version
  • Validation failure reason
  • Terminal status and retry attempt

Questions we investigate

  • Does technical completion satisfy business validation?
  • Which failure patterns recur after retries?
  • Are terminal statuses and eligibility consistent?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Add relevant outcome validation to completed jobs.
  • Fix repeated workflow and integration failures.
  • Set client-specific alerts and recovery ownership.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Automation operations lead
Daily for critical jobs; weekly for reliability review.

Required data

  • Unique eligible terminal job-attempt IDs
  • Validated outcome status and failure reasons
  • Retry links, workflow version, and terminal policy

Read the measure with context

Zero terminal attempts makes the rate undefined. Decide whether retries count as separate attempts; show eventual job resolution separately. Pending runs need a separate count. A technically completed run can still contain an incorrect or missing business outcome.
